title: Portion Size Without Tracking
summary: You don't need to weigh your food to eat sensible portions. A few visual anchors and environmental tweaks can make appropriate portions feel natural.

steps.heading: Why portion size matters more than food choice
steps.body: Research on overweight populations consistently finds that portion sizes have grown dramatically over the past 40 years — in restaurants, packaged food, and home cooking. Studies show that when people are served larger portions, they eat more without noticing or compensating at later meals. Portion size is one of the strongest predictors of total calorie intake, often more influential than which specific foods are chosen.

steps.heading: The hand as a measuring tool
steps.body: Your hand scales with your body size, making it a surprisingly accurate and always-available portion guide. Use a palm-sized portion for protein (meat, fish, tofu), a fist-sized portion for carbohydrates (rice, pasta, potatoes), a cupped handful for vegetables, and a thumb-tip for fats like butter or oil. This system won't be perfect — but it will be consistently reasonable.

steps.heading: Plate composition over calorie counting
steps.body: The plate method sidesteps the need for any tracking at all. Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables, a quarter with a quality protein source, and a quarter with a complex carbohydrate. This structure automatically moderates calorie density and delivers reasonable fibre and protein at every meal without arithmetic.

steps.heading: Environmental tricks that work
steps.body: You eat with your eyes before your stomach. Using smaller plates and bowls makes the same portion look more generous. Serving food in the kitchen rather than at the table reduces second helpings. Eating slowly and putting your fork down between bites gives your satiety hormones — which take 15–20 minutes to signal fullness — time to register before you over-serve yourself.

steps.heading: Eating out without overthinking
steps.body: Restaurant portions are typically 2–3 times a normal serving. Splitting a main with someone, ordering an entrée-sized portion rather than a main, or putting half the meal in a takeaway container before starting are all strategies that help. You don't need to analyse every dish — just eating half is often the simplest and most effective approach.

takeaway: Portion awareness is a practical skill, not a maths problem. Using visual anchors, structuring your plate, and making small environmental changes can bring portions under control without food scales, apps, or calorie labels.
